title: How to Know If You Should Marry Someone
excerpt: Nobody arrives at this decision with certainty. But there is a difference between healthy uncertainty and the doubt you are training yourself to ignore.
body:
People come to me before a wedding looking for permission, and what they usually want is for me to confirm a decision they have already made. Sometimes I can. Sometimes I sit there listening and realize they are asking me to silence a doubt they should be listening to instead. So let me say the thing first: nobody marries with certainty. If you are waiting to feel one hundred percent sure, you will wait forever, because marriage is a covenant made by two people who cannot see the future. The question is not whether you are certain. The question is whether your uncertainty is the ordinary kind or the warning kind.

## The questions worth more than feelings

Strip away the feeling for a moment and ask the structural questions, because these are the load-bearing walls of a marriage.

Do you respect them? Not just love, respect. Would you want to become more like this person? Marriage shapes you toward your spouse over the decades, and if you do not respect who they are, you are agreeing to be slowly shaped toward someone you do not admire.

Do they make your faith bigger or smaller? Not whether they are religious in the same way, but whether being near them draws you toward God or quietly away. Paul's instruction to marry in the Lord (1 Corinthians 7:39) is not snobbery. It is the recognition that you become one flesh, and one flesh cannot be split down the middle on the thing that matters most.

Can you fight well? Every marriage fights. The question is whether you can disagree and repair, or whether conflict turns into contempt and silence. Watch how you handle your worst moments together, not your best. The worst moments are the marriage you are actually signing up for.

## Listen to the people who love you

Here is a hard truth. The people who love you and are not in love can often see what you cannot. If your closest friends and your family are uneasy, and they are people of wisdom and not just protectiveness, do not dismiss them because your heart has already voted. Ask them directly: what do you see that I do not? Then sit in the discomfort of their answer.

I have rarely seen a marriage where everyone who loved the couple had serious reservations turn out to be a marriage they were glad they fought for. The voices of wise people around you are a gift God gives precisely because love makes you a poor judge of the person you love.

## The difference between cold feet and a real warning

Cold feet is fear of commitment itself, the weight of forever, the vertigo of choosing one life and closing others. That fear is normal and it is not a reason to stop. A real warning is different. A real warning is a specific, recurring thing you keep explaining away. The temper you keep excusing. The dishonesty you keep reframing as a quirk. The way they treat you when no one is watching that you keep telling yourself will change after the wedding.

It will not change after the wedding. Whatever you are tolerating now, you are agreeing to tolerate for life, often in a heavier dose. Marriage does not reform people. It magnifies what is already there. So ask honestly: is my hesitation about the size of the step, or about this specific person? Those are different feet getting cold.

## What you are actually promising

Marriage is not a reward for finding the right person. It is a promise to become the right person, to one specific human, through everything. The vow is not I will stay while you make me happy. It is I will stay (Ecclesiastes 4:9-12). So the final question is not only whether they are worth marrying. It is whether you are ready to be the kind of person who keeps a covenant when it costs.

## This week

Write down the one doubt you have been refusing to look at. Then ask one wise person who loves you, and is not afraid of you, to tell you the truth about your relationship. Let them finish before you defend anything.

You will not get certainty. You can get clarity. The difference between them is the difference between a feeling and a decision made with your eyes open.
